content:
According to reports, Apple is taking a new approach to bringing artificial intelligence features to Chinese users: training its own large language model with the assistance of Alibaba.

According to a Reuters report, three sources described this China-exclusive model as a departure from Apple's long-standing strategy of relying on third-party models.

The report stated that Alibaba assisted in training the model, but neither company responded to requests for comment.

Multiple models, including ChatGPT and Claude, are unavailable in mainland China, making Apple's current strategy in China differ from that in other major markets.

This development predates Alibaba's confirmation of its partnership with Apple in February 2025. Chinese internet regulators have also recently registered Apple Intelligence, allowing it to be used on the iPhone.

Earlier reports indicated that Alibaba's Qwen model and Baidu's technology would be integrated into this localised system.

Reuters noted that it remains unclear how Apple's new model will work with the aforementioned third-party models. The report stated that Apple Intelligence is expected to launch in China within the coming months following an iOS update.

Meanwhile, Apple's significantly revamped Siri AI features are expected to be publicly released this autumn with iOS 27, but only in regions where the service is available.

Initial support will be limited to specified English-language versions, and the rollout to iPhone and iPad in the European Union will be delayed. The launch timeline for the Chinese market has yet to be determined.
